Hi @Pieter64 — an update on this issue: the fixes are now included in the new test candidate [v0.6.2-rc.2](https://github.com/Vituhlos/ha-ikea-bilresa/releases/tag/v0.6.2-rc.2). This also includes a couple of additional fixes unrelated to the light-group behavior.

Could you try it with the same setup you reported (HA Core 2026.10.2, Zigbee2MQTT 2.7.2, 3–4 bulbs, step 3, perceptual curve, minimum 1, transition 0.8) and let us know whether the stale brightness jumps are gone and slow, small-batch scrolling feels smoother? It's still a test pre-release, and we haven't validated the fix against your exact group setup yet. Thanks again for the detailed report!

*🤖 Agent-assisted: this comment was written by Claude, an AI assistant working on this repository with the maintainer (@Vituhlos), who read and approved it before it was posted.*

Hi @Pieter64 👋 a short follow-up: the pre-release **v0.7.0-rc.6** is out, and it contains everything from `v0.6.2-rc.2` that we asked you to try (the fixes for stale brightness jumps with a group entity), plus a binding that can **dim several individual bulbs from one tracked level**.

**🧪 Not verified for your setup.** We have never tried your exact group (HA 2026.10.2, Zigbee2MQTT 2.7.2, 3–4 bulbs, step 3, perceptual curve, minimum 1, transition 0.8), and the new multi-light binding is related to your problem but not proven to fix it.

**❓ Two questions**
1. With the group entity as the target, do the jumps to unrelated brightness levels still happen in rc.6 (or in rc.2, if you tried it)?
2. If they do, would you also try the same channel with the **individual bulbs** as targets instead of the group? That is the case the new binding was made for, and your answer would be the first real test of it 🙏

<details>
<summary>How to install v0.7.0-rc.6</summary>

- **Home Assistant 2026.11 and newer (Marketplace, where HACS has moved):** Settings → Marketplace → IKEA BILRESA → ⋮ → *Install another version* → `v0.7.0-rc.6`, then restart Home Assistant.
- **Older Home Assistant (HACS):** HACS → IKEA BILRESA → ⋮ → Redownload → enable "Show beta versions" → `v0.7.0-rc.6`, then restart Home Assistant.

It is a pre-release, so take a backup first. A binding that runs actions, or one with several lights, is stored in a form that `0.7.0-rc.5` and earlier do not read in full.
</details>

**Waiting for you:** we have marked this issue as waiting for information. If we do not hear back, it may be closed after some weeks; it can be reopened at any time, and nothing is lost.

🤖 Agent-authored: Claude Code, model `claude-sonnet-5-5`

item.title: Brightness binding jumps to stale levels when the target is a Zigbee2MQTT light group; single notches get no transition

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Waiting for the reporter's logs, version or answer

item.body:
Setup: v0.6.0 · HA 2026.10.2 (HAOS) · BILRESA scroll wheel (E2490) over Thread · targets are Zigbee2MQTT 2.7.2 group entities (3–4 bulbs each) · brightness mode, step 3, perceptual curve, min 1, transition 0.8

1. Jumps to unrelated brightness levels mid-scroll
While scrolling, the brightness occasionally jumps to a different level, usually much brighter than the levels just before and after it. The group entity received about 180 state updates in 10 minutes of testing. Z2M passes each member bulb’s own brightness report up to the group as the bulbs fade, so the group’s reported brightness wanders. I believe _is_own_echo() treats these as values outside the expected path, and _forget_target("unrecognized_value_during_scroll") then rebases onto the stale value. Your docstring already mentions this (“Deliberately unaddressed: a light group reports the average of its members…”), but Z2M groups don’t report an average: they report whichever member reported last.
Suggestion: an option per binding to never rebase during an active scroll (trust the tracked target until _RESYNC_AFTER), or to rebase only after the target has been quiet for N ms.

2. Single-notch batches are never faded
_smoothing_transition() returns 0 for notches <= 1 and scales the transition by notches / 14. Slow scrolling produces mostly 1–3 notch batches, so even with transition 0.8 s the dimming looks steppy. I understand the first notch is unfaded on purpose for responsiveness.
Suggestion: an option to apply the full configured transition to every batch (or to every batch after the first in a gesture).

Workaround I’m using: removed the bindings and drive the lights from the per-channel dial entities with an HA automation (fixed 0.6 s transition, plus a sync-back automation with a 3 s quiet window). It works well, which suggests the event pipeline is solid and only the binding’s echo and smoothing logic struggles with groups.
